sector_model: nonfinancial: animal health pharma; EPS, FCF yield, net debt/EBITDA-style leverage, organic growth by franchise
thesis: Zoetis (animal health leader) closed 79.40 on 2026-11-06 (-11% over two sessions after Q3 results on 11-05, from 89.20 on 11-04). Market cap about 32.3B on 406,316,147 shares (10-Q cover, 2026-10-30). TTM GAAP EPS about 5.93 gives about 13.4x; 2026 adjusted EPS guide 6.25 to 6.35 (raised) gives about 12.6x management-adjusted. TTM operating cash flow 2.73B less capex 0.49B = FCF 2.24B, a 6.9% yield on market cap. Net debt about 7.5B (9.05B debt less 1.33B cash and 0.2B short-term investments). The market appears to price a structural decline in U.S. companion animal (Q3 -8% organic, dermatology -15.7%) from competition, generics and price sensitivity, while international (+3.9% Q3, +9.3% 9M), livestock (+6.8%) and vaccines (+5.5%) grow.
counterthesis: U.S. segment revenue fell 5.8% in Q3 and 6.7% in 9M; dermatology (Apoquel/Cytopoint franchise) fell 15.7% and management cites competitive pressure and generics, which may be permanent erosion of the highest-margin franchise rather than cyclical softness. GAAP net income fell 18% in Q3 (591M vs 721M) with a 78M intangible impairment and 43M restructuring; reported 2026 EPS guidance was lowered (5.50 to 5.60) while adjusted was raised, so the adjusted figure excludes recurring-looking charges (9M restructuring 142M). Cash fell from 2.45B to 1.33B while 1.69B of buybacks and 666M of dividends were paid; debt is 9.05B including 750M current, so buybacks are effectively debt/cash-funded. A pending Neogen genomics deal and a derivative suit add uncertainty. FCF yield uses 9M operating cash flow that benefited from working capital which was not examined.
invalidation: U.S. companion animal declines continuing past -8% organic for two more quarters; dermatology share loss widening; adjusted EPS guide cut; FCF below dividends plus interest; net leverage rising above about 3x EBITDA; further intangible impairments; evidence that the adjusted-to-GAAP gap is recurring.
